Comments:
Constructed from your organisation's IATI identifier and a string of your choice to identify the activity. 

Once you have published an activity, its IATI identifier will not change.
Unique identifier and name of organisation reporting the activity.
A short title to describe the activity.
A longer description that explains what the activity is (minimum short paragraph).
A description of which stage of implementation the activity is currently at. As the activity progresses over time, the activity status should be updated.
The start and end dates of the activity. Start dates may reflect the beginning of funding, planning or physical activity. End dates should, wherever possible, reflect the ending of physical activity.
Information on the sector(s) that the activity targets or supports, such as primary education or agriculture. Use OECD DAC 5-digit sector codes, where possible.

Funding - the organisation(s) funding the project.

Implementing - the organisation carrying out the actual work of the project.

Accountable - the organisation responsible for managing the delivery of the project.

The country or countries that benefit from the activity – i.e. where impact is felt. These should be eligible for Official Development Assistance (ODA) and may differ from the location of the activity.

Regions can be specified instead of, or as well as, individual countries. When using percentages, all percentages across countries and regions must add up to 100%
Contact information for the activity. You can add multiple points of contact if needed.
The sub-national location of an activity, if known and safe to disclose. You can provide geographic coordinates, an administrative area, or general description.
Documents relating to the activity such as a project proposal, Theory of Change, or annual report.
